teams.heading: Fiji prop up the Nations Championship standings after third consecutive defeat
teams.body: Fiji prop up the Nations Championship standings in bottom place after failing to secure a point from their opening three fixtures. The Flying Fijians have now suffered three straight defeats, including a 17-33 loss to Scotland at home in the previous round in July 2026. Across their last five international matches, the side has registered just one victory alongside four defeats. With a point difference of -96 from 49 points scored and 145 conceded, the squad faces a steep climb.

teams.heading: Maro Itoje backs Steve Borthwick's surprise decision to grant summer sabbatical
teams.body: England captain Maro Itoje has endorsed head coach Steve Borthwick's surprise decision to omit him from the July tour, admitting the mental recovery was far more significant than the physical benefit. Itoje rested during the Nations Championship fixtures against South Africa, Fiji and Argentina after exceeding recommended match limits in consecutive seasons. Having also dealt with the loss of his mother, the lock initially found the sabbatical proposal shocking but now feels revitalised. "I don't regret it at all," Itoje said, targeting a strong run.

teams.heading: France beat Japan but remain far from their historic ranking peak
teams.body: France currently sit third out of 12 teams in the standings after three fixtures. A convincing 42-15 victory against Japan in the third round secured their second win. Les Bleus have registered 116 points in those three games, whilst conceding 75 points. Although they boast a positive point difference of 41 from their fixtures, they remain far from their historical peak. The team's longest unbroken spell at number one in the world rankings lasted for just one week, back in July 2022.

teams.heading: Vascular injury rules fly-half Jack Crowley out of Ireland’s autumn internationals
teams.body: Ireland’s fly-half options are depleted ahead of the November internationals, with Jack Crowley ruled out until the new year. The 26-year-old playmaker has been sidelined since April with a lower limb vascular injury, forcing him to miss July's Tests and the upcoming autumn fixtures. It is a major setback for Munster and the national side. Munster boss Clayton McMillan emphasised a cautious approach, stating that "ensuring he gets back to 100% is the priority."

teams.heading: Timothy Lafaele and naturalised players force League One eligibility rule U-turn
teams.body: Japan Rugby League One has watered down its controversial player eligibility changes following a legal challenge from 25 foreign-born players, including Timothy Lafaele. The players had filed for a court injunction against rules that restricted matchday squad spots for naturalised citizens who lacked six years of Japanese schooling. Under the settled terms, naturalised players holding citizenship since May 2025 or earlier will avoid these limits. Additionally, any player with 30 or more caps for the Brave Blossoms will be reclassified to Category A-1.

lead.why: The JRLO's significant eligibility rule climbdown resolves a high-profile legal battle involving several prominent Brave Blossoms.

teams.heading: Nick Mallett accuses All Blacks of deliberately collapsing scrums to cheat Springboks
teams.body: Former Springboks coach Nick Mallett has accused the All Blacks of deliberately collapsing scrums to negate South Africa's powerful front row. Speaking after the Boks' 33-26 victory in Cape Town, he claimed New Zealand routinely take the set-piece to the ground because they lack the personnel to match the hosts' power. The accusation intensifies the war of words between Dave Rennie and Rassie Erasmus ahead of Saturday's third Test in Soweto, following earlier disputes over South Africa's scrumming angles.

teams.heading: Daan Human denies All Blacks scrum cheating accusations before Johannesburg rematch
teams.body: Springboks assistant coach Daan Human has hit back at Dave Rennie’s claims that South Africa use illegal "walking around" tactics to dominate the scrum. Ahead of Saturday's third Test in Johannesburg, Human insisted the world champions strive for "legal, straightforward dominance," adding: "I can't ever cheat or tell the players to walk around – we never work like that." Nick Mallett supported the stance, suggesting referee Angus Gardner had preconceived notions in Cape Town. South Africa levelled the series with a 33-26 victory last weekend.
